| Regulatory basis | • Commercial-space managers or operators should provide complete, compliant collection containers; failure requires correction and may attract fines. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 44, [D-06-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering or stockpiling violates Article 16 and attracts CNY 5,000–50,000 fines for organisations and up to CNY 200 for individuals under Article 42. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 16, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Commercial spaces fall within the guidance for classification, collection and management; unlisted settings should follow similar functional areas and meet current national and local standards. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 1.2, [D-16-C001](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Shopping-centre and other public-facility operators should provide supporting collection facilities; failure may constitute a violation. Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China, Article 510, paragraph 1, [D-01-C003](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Spitting, public urination or defecation and littering are prohibited. Scattered bags, foam boxes and cardboard fall within this prohibition and may attract penalties if caused by individuals or businesses. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 27, items (1), [D-06-C006](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Five accumulations, including temporary foam-box storage, scattered items and slippery ground, affect appearance and pedestrian safety and involve improper stockpiling. No bins overflow. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects: poor pavement sanitation and piles affect safe passage, particularly on slippery ground. Foam boxes occupy public space and impair the commercial image. Near-term risks: businesses or residents may imitate the practice; delayed clearance may encourage insects and odours and reduce environmental quality. |
| Potential causes | • Businesses or delivery workers may leave packaging temporarily: JD Express cartons, bottles and cardboard around the foam box suggest delivery activity. Check whether the area is a delivery or temporary storage point.<br>• Container provision or collection may be inadequate: two non-overflowing bins coexist with five accumulations. Check allocation standards and collection records.<br>• Supervision may be inadequate: prolonged foam-box storage and no visible prohibition signs suggest management gaps. Check notices and classification guidance. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could worsen sanitation, commercial appearance and customer experience; accumulation may cause fire risks or vector breeding. Delayed correction may attract penalties and higher costs, while a ‘broken windows’ effect could encourage further violations. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: clear accumulations, especially the S13-B-02 foam box and surrounding items; restore clean paving; clean and maintain intact bins; and add prominent notices against stockpiling.<br>• Longer-term action: increase bins or provide temporary storage points, optimise collection, educate businesses and delivery staff about classification and storage, and establish daily checks with prompt advice or reporting of violations. |
| Priority | **Medium.** Multiple accumulations and improper storage affect appearance and public safety without severe pollution or an emergency. Prioritise correction within the routine check cycle. |
